subject: Private cluster: preflight sizing & IO profiling for SwiftHealth pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@swifthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster: preflight sizing & IO profiling for SwiftHealth pilot

Hi Nora,

Thanks again for the time today. As we discussed, the pilot will run a single private Kubernetes cluster in your DC-3 site and host two main workloads: a model-serving fleet (GPU-backed inference pods) and a smaller control plane of side services (logging, metrics, cache). Before we lock a node count I want to make sure we align on the IO profile and fault domain expectations.

Quick checklist I need from your team to finalize a proposal:
- Typical batch size/requests per second for the inference service (p50/p95).
- Average and peak token lengths per request (these affect GPU memory & KV cache behavior).
- Expected model sizes (checked-point sizes, quantized vs fp16) and whether you expect to swap models frequently.
- SAN vs local NVMe preference for model artifacts and KV cache.
- RPO/RTO goals for node failures (how quickly must inference traffic recover, and acceptable grace windows).

I've copied Ben (nodepool sizing) and Neha (storage & networking) so they can propose a concrete node mix once we have the IO numbers. We're aiming to keep the pilot to a single AZ footprint initially but design for multi-rack failure isolation.

Plan: once we have metrics from you, Redwood will produce a nodepool layout (gpu-heavy, burst, control) and an IO mapping doc with recommended PV classes and retention rules. We can then do a 48-hour soak on the proposed topology in our staging cluster with synthetic workloads that mimic your p95 tails.

Can you share the short matrix by EOD Monday? I've attached a quick template you can paste into (swifthealth-mat-reqs.xlsx).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-8123

Attachment: swifthealth-mat-reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet - matrix of RPS, token lengths, model sizes)
From: Nora Patel <nora@swifthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: SwiftHealth Infra Team <infra@swifthealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: preflight sizing & IO profiling for SwiftHealth pilot

Marissa —

Thanks for the template and the call. Quick answers below (our infra lead also copied):

- Traffic: steady-state 35 RPS (small baseline), spikes up to 420 RPS for 10-15 min windows (daily batch ingest). p95 latency target for inference = 120ms.
- Tokens: average 120 tokens / request, p95 ~ 680 tokens.
- Models: primary model is a 14B parameter family (quantized fp16 artifacts ~ 28GB), we will try a smaller 7B for fallbacks. Model swaps expected every 4–6 weeks for fine-tune rollouts.
- Storage: prefer local NVMe for KV cache and model artifacts to minimize network egress, but we need persistence for artifact archive on NFS/SAN for long-term snapshots.
- RPO/RTO: RTO target is 3 minutes for degraded throughput (graceful fallback to smaller model or hosted variant), full recovery 30 minutes.

We filled the spreadsheet and attached it. Also included are our current monitoring sample traces for a peak day.

Nora Patel
Platform Ops, SwiftHealth
infra@swifthealth.com

Attachment: swifthealth-mat-reqs.xlsx (completed)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora@swifthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2026 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: preflight sizing & IO profiling for SwiftHealth pilot

Folks —

Thanks, Nora, this is helpful. From the numbers I'd propose the following initial node pools (pilot):

1) gpu-prod (3 x A100-80GB equiv) - steady inference: 2 nodes schedulable for 12 concurrent containers each, reserve 10% for system and model prewarm. This assumes your 14B quantized model fits in ~28GB GPU memory; we’ll prefer 80GB class to keep headroom for kv caches.

2) gpu-burst (2 x A100-80GB equiv) - autoscale enabled for peak periods, preemptible/backfill capable to reduce cost.

3) control (3 x 8CPU, 32GB RAM) - runs ingress, logging, autoscaler, and a small stateful sidecar for local KV coordination.

Storage mapping:
- Model artifacts and KV cache -> local NVMe PV (fastest hot path) with a scheduled nightly rsync to a resilient SAN NFS for snapshots.
- Persistent metadata (configs, backups) -> NFS with replication across racks.

Networking / failure domains:
- Single AZ pilot but 3 rack-distributed failure domains; kube-proxy in IPVS mode; BGP routing for external egress.
- We suggest GRACEFUL drain windows of 90s with AI-serving readiness probes that allow existing in-flight requests to finish.

Next steps from infra: Neha can produce a PV class matrix and a proposed CSI config for NVMe and NFS. If SwiftHealth is OK with the 80GB GPU class we draft an Installation Plan and a short soak test spec (48h synthetic workload that replicates your p95 tails).

Ben
Ben Carter | Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@swifthealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private cluster: preflight sizing & IO profiling for SwiftHealth pilot

All —

Appreciate the quick turn. Summary / action items so we're aligned before I send the formal proposal: 

1) Node pools: gpu-prod (3 x 80GB), gpu-burst (2 x 80GB, preemptible), control (3 x small). Ben will draft deployment manifests with taints/tolerations and HPA config.
2) Storage: NVMe for hot models + nightly rsync to SAN NFS. Neha to share PVClass/CSI notes and recommended mount options (noatime, discard where supported).
3) Failure & recovery: RTO/RPO as stated by SwiftHealth; implement model fallback route to 7B family plus a hosted fallback policy. We'll include automatic traffic steering in the Canary plan.
4) Soak test: 48h synthetic with two injected peak windows (15 min each) that hit 420 RPS. We'll schedule the soak in our staging cluster the week of Oct 18.

I've attached our initial nodepool proposal PDF (redwood-nodepool-proposal-v1.pdf) with the expected resource requests/limits and kubelet tuning. Please review and confirm by EOD Wed so we can get procurement a rough cost estimate for the pilot.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-nodepool-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal - node counts, kubelet flags, CSI settings)
